newsitem.title: USA: U.S Senate panel subpoenas fund-raiser wife's records.
newsitem.headline: U.S Senate panel subpoenas fund-raiser wife's records.

text.p: The Senate panel probing campaign fund-raising scandals Tuesday announced it had issued another batch of 26 subpoenas, including a request for records of Jane Huang, whose husband is a key figure in the probe.

Most of the other subpoenas were for various banks, in what a Senate Government Affairs Committee aide said was an attempt to trace some campaign donations. Some but not all the banks may have records pertaining to Asian-American donors.

The committee is investigating an assortment of alleged illegalities in the 1996 elections, including whether China and other foreign interests sought to influence U.S. foreign policy by helping President Bill Clinton and the Democratic Party with illegal political contributions.
The FBI and a House committee were conducting simultaneous but separate investigations.

Jane Huang was one of three individuals listed in the latest batch of subpoenas. She is the wife of John Huang, a former Commerce Department official and former Democratic National Committee official. The panel is seeking records about any possible fund-raising activities by her while he was a Commerce official.

Also on the list was Man Ho, identified as an official at the Hsi Lai Temple, the Buddhist temple that was the site of a controversial fundraiser attended by Vice President Al Gore. The temple has tax-free status and is supposed to be nonpolitical.
